name: Ohio
overview: Ohio mostly sells tax-delinquent real estate outright after a tax foreclosure. A court orders the parcel sold, and the county sheriff sells it, usually online through the state's sheriff sale auction site run by RealAuction under a state contract. In a tax foreclosure the minimum bid can be the taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs owed rather than the usual two-thirds of appraised value. Parcels left unsold after two sales are forfeited to the state, and the county auditor can later offer them at a forfeited land sale. Some county treasurers also sell tax certificates (liens): at a public auction, bidding starts at 18% simple interest per year and goes down. Some counties, such as Franklin, instead sell their certificates in bulk as a portfolio.

counties.office: Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department, Civil Division
counties.next_sale_note: No specific sale dates or recurring sale day are posted on the official pages read. The Sheriff assigns each sale date roughly six weeks after an order of sale. An older county 'topics' page (https://cuyahogacounty.gov/topics/foreclosure-sales) says 'Foreclosure sales are conducted every Monday at 9:00 a.m.' at the Justice Center, but it conflicts with the current online-only pages and is treated as outdated.
counties.how_to_bid: All sheriff foreclosure sales, tax-delinquent ones included, are held online only through the county's RealAuction site, where bidders register and must meet RealAuction's terms. Buyers of tax-delinquent properties must file an Affidavit of Non-delinquency for each property. Payment goes to the Sheriff's Civil Division by certified or cashier's check, money order or law firm check.

sources.terms: County disclaimer covers accuracy only ('Cuyahoga County does not guarantee the accuracy or timeliness of this information'). No copying, scraping or commercial-use restriction found.

evidence.quote: All Cuyahoga County Sheriff Foreclosure Sales are held online only.
The Sheriff will assign a sale date approximately six weeks from the date an order of sale is issued.
The purchaser is required to submit an Affidavit of Non-delinquency for EACH property.

counties.office: Franklin County Sheriff's Office, Real Estate Sales Unit
counties.address: 373 South High Street, Floor 2B, Attn: Real Estate, Columbus, OH 43215
counties.schedule_rule: Our Sheriff Sales are held every Friday morning at 9:00 a.m. online
counties.next_sale_note: No specific sale dates posted on the official pages. Sheriff sales run weekly on Fridays except federal holidays. Separately, the Treasurer sells tax lien certificates as a single bulk portfolio; the last date posted was November 3, 2025 (past), and the Treasurer says the sale is 'generally held in October each year'. No 2026 or 2027 lien sale date is posted.
counties.how_to_bid: Bidders register with RealAuction, complete the Purchaser Information Form and post the minimum deposit ($2,000, $5,000 or $10,000, set by law) before the weekly Friday online auction. Bids start at two-thirds of appraised value. The sheriff page says tax sales may also be held on location at 373 S. High St. The Treasurer's lien certificate sale is a single bundled portfolio, not an auction of individual certificates.

counties.office: Hamilton County Sheriff's Office, Civil Enforcement Unit
counties.schedule_rule: Hamilton County Sheriff's Property Sales are held on Wednesday at 11:00 am
counties.next_sale_note: No specific sale dates posted on the official page.
counties.how_to_bid: Sheriff sales have been online through RealAuction since 1/1/2024, with registration and deposits handled there. The deposit is $5,000 for residential property valued at $200,000 or less and $10,000 above that. Delinquent-tax sales are described as a live auction in Room 260 of the Hamilton County Courthouse, paid in full by cashier's check at the time of sale. Tax lien certificate sales cover parcels whose liens were sold in bulk to a third party.

counties.office: Summit County Sheriff's Office, Civil Division
counties.schedule_rule: DELINQUENT TAX SALES are held on Tuesdays at 10:00am.
counties.next_sale_note: No specific sale dates posted on the official pages.
counties.how_to_bid: Bidders register on the Sheriff's RealAuction site, get a bidder number and post a $1,000.00 deposit for each delinquent tax sale case before the sale. The highest bidder wins, and the balance is due within thirty days after the Confirmation Order is filed. Tax-foreclosure buyers must file an affidavit under ORC 5721.19(J); the page also says a person who owns property in Ohio cannot buy through a tax foreclosure sale.
